title: Hole plant stations for planting macadamia trees

lessons.title: Getting ready to dig
lessons.html:
What is holing?

Holing means digging a hole at each peg where a macadamia tree will be planted. A good hole gives the young tree's roots loose soil to grow into. A bad hole can make the tree grow slowly or die.

Find the peg

  • Each peg marks one tree.
  • The hole must be dug with the peg in the centre.
  • Do not lose the peg. It shows the exact spot.

Use a planting board

A planting board is a long plank with a notch in the middle and a hole or notch at each end.

  1. Put the middle notch against the peg.
  2. Put a small peg in each end hole.
  3. Lift the board away. Take out the centre peg.
  4. Dig the hole.
  5. Later, put the board back on the two end pegs. The middle notch shows the exact centre for the tree.

Your tools

  • Spade
  • Pick for hard soil
  • Crowbar for stones
  • Planting board and small pegs
  • Measuring stick for depth and width

Check that your tools are in good condition. A loose pick head is dangerous. Tell your supervisor if a tool is broken.

Your PPE

  • Safety boots
  • Gloves
  • Hat and sunscreen

Drink water often. Rest in the shade when you can.

lessons.title: Digging the hole
lessons.html:
How big?

Your supervisor will tell you the size of the hole. On many farms the soil is prepared with a ridger or ripper first, and the hole is a little bigger than the bag of the young tree. Use the measuring stick to check width and depth.

Steps

  1. Clear grass and weeds from around the spot.
  2. Dig the top soil out first. It is darker. Put it on one side of the hole.
  3. Dig the deeper soil (subsoil). It is lighter. Put it on the other side.
  4. Keep the sides of the hole rough. Smooth, hard sides stop roots from growing out. Break them with the spade.
  5. Loosen the bottom of the hole.
  6. Take out big stones and roots.
  7. Check the size with the measuring stick.
  8. If the supervisor says so, mix compost or fertiliser with the topsoil. Use the amount you are given.

Do not

  • Do not dig when the soil is very wet. It becomes hard and smooth.
  • Do not put the subsoil back on top.
  • Do not leave open holes where people or animals walk at night without telling the supervisor. Someone can fall in.

Safety

  • Stand with feet apart. Keep your back straight.
  • Keep other workers at a safe distance when you swing a pick.
  • Look for snakes, scorpions and buried pipes or cables. If you hit a pipe or cable, stop and call the supervisor.

Finish

Tell the supervisor how many holes you dug. Clean your tools and put them away.

Key points

  • Dig the hole with the peg in the centre. Use a planting board.
  • Put topsoil on one side and subsoil on the other side.
  • Make the sides rough, not smooth.
  • Check the size with the measuring stick.
  • Keep others away when you swing a pick.
